extracted.intended_audience: third-party stakeholders and organisations with an interest in EFSA's work (food and feed sector), including organisations considering registration to engage with EFSA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing who counts as an EFSA stakeholder and how stakeholders should engage with EFSA (registration, engagement principles, domains, platforms, and how input is used). Intended for organisations and other third parties wishing to participate in EFSA processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders are third parties that have an interest in the Authority’s work or in the wider food and feed sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the pool of potential participants who may engage with EFSA and underpins eligibility for non‑registered engagement routes and for registering as a stakeholder organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders are classified into seven categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFSA organises stakeholders into seven categories (page references the classification) to structure engagement; the classification determines roles, relationships and potentially which engagement mechanisms are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration (optional) and access benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is not mandatory, but registered organisations have access to a combination of standing and ad‑hoc engagement platforms as well as the mechanisms available to non‑registered stakeholders and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations may register to engage more closely with EFSA; registration provides additional channels and opportunities for targeted involvement but is voluntary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement principle — Trustworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement is designed to safeguard EFSA’s objectivity and independence. EFSA aims to foster trustworthy relations by engaging stakeholders based on the relevance of their interests and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFSA pursues a balanced representation of interests to prevent specific communities exerting any undue influence through the interactive mechanisms. Whenever targeted engagement is needed to focus on specific interest groups and expertise, this is conducted with full transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement principle — Targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement is a targeted process that gives stakeholders the opportunity to contribute their experience in their field of interest and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A targeted approach ensures stakeholders focus on activities where they can add and extract value; it provides flexibility important for a dynamic environment with shifting priorities, emerging issues, or new demands from risk managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement principle — Traceable
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement is embedded in EFSA’s scientific process and planning. EFSA identifies stakeholder contributions and maps how those contributions were made and considered or incorporated in its scientific outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFSA continuously improves tools and processes so stakeholders can trace how their input was used to inform EFSA’s advice to policymakers. Examples include tracing outcomes of public consultations and improving accessibility via Open.EFSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain — Foresight and preparedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizon scanning and foresight activities so EFSA can stay relevant for policymakers and EU citizens, and be prepared for the challenges ahead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder input supports anticipating future issues and informing preparedness plans; engagement here is aimed at high‑level, forward‑looking evidence and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain — Risk assessment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic‑based engagement on EFSA’s mandates and applications to improve the quality and transparency of EFSA’s scientific advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders can provide evidence and information to support EFSA’s scientific risk assessments; engagement is open to public scrutiny and input is considered in line with openness and transparency principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain — Dialogue with stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Open dialogue between EFSA and stakeholders to build mutual understanding of roles, responsibilities and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue is used to develop shared understanding rather than to replace formal assessment processes; it supports relationship‑building and clarifying expectations among parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stakeholder input
rubrics_metrics.description: Input from stakeholders is used to identify issues requiring EFSA’s preparedness and to inform new mandates, to support EFSA’s scientific risk assessment with relevant evidence, and to improve the mechanisms through which EFSA engages with stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFSA commits to enhancing traceability of stakeholder input (e.g., outcomes of public consultations) and accessibility of information (e.g., Open.EFSA) to ensure openness and transparency in how input informs policy advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement platforms and mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: EFSA provides a catalogue of engagement mechanisms, tools, resources and services, and describes the contexts in which they are activated (including engagement in risk assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This catalogue helps stakeholders identify appropriate channels (standing/ad‑hoc platforms, calls, consultations) and understand expectations for participation; EFSA stresses that scientific risk assessment engagement is open to public scrutiny and stakeholder input in full compliance with openness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls for stakeholders / Thematic communities
rubrics_metrics.description: EFSA may launch calls for expression of interest to build thematic communities of stakeholders with an interest in a given topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such calls are a mechanism to assemble targeted groups of expertise for specific topics; participation may depend on relevance, expertise and (for deeper engagement) registration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and support (questions and resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: EFSA provides ways to ask questions and access related stakeholder news, events, and lists of registered stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFSA offers support channels for clarification and signposts resources to help stakeholders understand engagement opportunities and administrative processes (e.g., how to register, where to find consultation outcomes).
